ordered_diagnoses: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin condition with laxity and coalesced papules, primarily affecting flexural areas, with a long-standing history and familial involvement
salient_findings: Progressive skin laxity with severe sagging
Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules in flexural areas
Excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments in the reticular dermis
key_facts: 20-year history of progressive skin laxity
Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules developed in early childhood
Skin sagging occurred on the abdomen with loss of elasticity
Condition spread extensively with developmental growth
No extracutaneous involvement
Born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents
Younger sister had the same skin symptoms
Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%)
Prolonged prothrombin time (12.8 seconds)
Echocardiographic examination results were normal
Fundoscopic examination results were normal
Compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene
